questions.question: What is a median of a random variable $X$?
options: The largest possible value of $X$
A real number $m$ with $P(X\le m)\ge1/2$ and $P(X\ge m)\ge1/2$
The expected squared deviation from the mean
The only value where the density is zero
questions.explanation: A median is any real $m$ with $P(X\le m)\ge 1/2$ and $P(X\ge m)\ge 1/2$: it balances probability half on each side.
questions.source_support: The definition states $P(X\le m)\ge1/2$ and $P(X\ge m)\ge1/2$.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
option_explanations: The maximum is a support endpoint, not the balancing point that splits probability in half.
That is the variance, a spread measure, not the median.
A density-zero point is not the median; the median balances probability half-and-half.

questions.source_support: The interpretation says a median splits the distribution into two balanced parts.
option_explanations: Maximizing variance is unrelated; the median splits probability evenly.
Counting arrivals is a process operation; the median is a $50\%$ probability split.

questions.question: For a continuous strictly increasing CDF, where is the median?
